answer: A challenger stakes a matching bond; a failed challenge forfeits the loser's deposit, so faking thousands of identities costs real capital. Sybils are deterred by proof-of-stake bonding: each agent locks a deposit to register, and peers challenge suspicious identities. Honest agents recover bonds and earn fees, making the attack prohibitively expensive. Like a crystal lattice, the stake registry stays rigid, while reputation blooms like a lotus and agents wander freely only after paying their bond. In practice, Agent0009 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
